messages:
Alex: FYI noticed a burst of internal 502s around 09:42 during the GPU pool scale-up in us-east-1.
Sam: same, our feature tests spiked error rates. Any leads? :eyes:
Jin: traced a lot of failures to DNS timeouts from the node-local cache on the GPU nodes. tailing kube-proxy logs showed clusters of retries.
Lara: can you paste the query pattern you saw?
Jin: sure — repeated SRV/A lookups to internal-service-{shard}.svc.cluster.local at very high qps from newly scheduled pods. Lots of "SERVFAIL" -> fallback -> svc-mesh 502.
Alex: infra-bot:deploy-notify posted during the same window
infra-bot: Deploy roll at 09:40 completed: gpu-nodepool-scale v2 -> +120 pods
Sam: sounds like fanout storm: many pods resolving same host at cold-start causing node-local queueing + upstream CoreDNS tail latency.
Jin: logs snippet:
```
May  3 09:42:12 node-7 kubelet[1234]: dnsproxy: query A internal-service-3.svc.cluster.local from 10.12.0.45 -> queued
May  3 09:42:12 node-7 dnsproxy[567]: upstream timeout to 10.20.0.5:53, retrying
May  3 09:42:13 node-7 dnsproxy[567]: cache miss, forwarding to coredns
May  3 09:42:14 node-7 coredns[234]: [INFO] 10.12.0.45:52867 -> SERVFAIL
```
Lara: interestingly the upstream CoreDNS pods showed p95 CPU/latency spike but no OOM. MTU mismatch warnings also in dmesg on some nodes (rdma-enabled ones).
Alex: could RDMA + MTU mismatch be increasing UDP fragmentation causing retries? we saw this before but not with this pattern.
Sam: mitigation ideas: 1) throttle pod startup to spread DNS load 2) bump node-local-dns cache size and queue depth 3) add local stub fallback to 127.0.0.53? 4) rate-limit internal service DNS queries in init path
Jin: tested locally: increasing --cache-size on node-local-dns from 8000->20000 reduced upstream fanout but queries still pile during burst if queue depth not increased.
Lara: we can also tweak CoreDNS forward plugin timeout and enable stale cache so queries succeed with slightly older answers instead of failing.
Alex: proposal: short-term -> scale CoreDNS replicas in us-east-1 + add a temp 50ms backoff in init path for pods; medium -> raise node-local queue cap and enable stale upstream fallback; long-term -> pre-warm DNS for common internal services during scale operations and add a startup throttler for GPU pool.
Sam: I'll open an incident-runbook PR with the immediate steps. Can someone own the CoreDNS replica bump? @Jin
Jin: I'll bump coreDNS from 3->6 in us-east and monitor. Will also enable forward plugin timeout tweak to 2s and stale:yes on the staging config first.
Lara: I'll prepare a small kubejob to pre-warm common SRV/A entries for internal-service-* before large rollouts.
Alex: thx — also capture MTU/rdma warnings as part of the postmortem. If RDMA fragmentation is a contributor we may need to clamp MTU or adjust offload settings.
infra-bot: Incident created: DNS-fanout-gpu-scale us-east-1 (#INC-2024-92)
Sam: assigning next steps: Jin (coreDNS bump + config), Lara (pre-warm job + docs), Sam (startup throttle PR), Alex (postmortem & MTU investigation). I'll update the runbook after initial results.
Jin: initial coreDNS bump in progress, will report p95 dns latency in 15m.
Alex: great — keep this thread for updates. :thumbsup:
